title: Doppel report: fake Black Friday deals began appearing on 1 September, over a month earlier than last year
date_note: Help Net Security's publication day; the page gives no earlier day for Doppel's findings.
summary: Help Net Security, relaying research by security firm Doppel, reports that this year's fake Black Friday deals started appearing on September 1, more than a month earlier than last year. Doppel says about one in four lookalike pages are hosted on legitimate platforms such as Google Sites, Blogger and GitHub Pages, and that 99.7% of confirmed fraudulent ads ran on Facebook Ads.
plain: Security firm Doppel says fake Black Friday shopping pages and ads began appearing on September 1, more than a month earlier than last year, and many sit on well-known hosting sites.
exec: Doppel's research, as reported by Help Net Security, says fake Black Friday deals started on September 1, more than a month earlier than last year, so seasonal brand-impersonation risk starts earlier.
action: General advice: do not rely on a web address containing a brand name as proof a page is genuine, and treat login prompts on sale pages with caution; no page read gives Doppel's own advice.
geo_basis: none: the report names no single location
